title: kith-jmap: JMAP error response formatting
description:
JMAP error response formatting: map errors to method-level and request-level JMAP wire format.

What: Implement helper functions that convert errors to the correct JMAP wire format — method-level (error Invocation in methodResponses) and request-level (HTTP 4xx with JMAP error body).

Algorithm:
1. Define pub fn error_invocation(method_name: &str, call_id: &str, err: JmapError) -> Invocation
   - Returns (method_name.to_string(), serde_json::to_value(err).unwrap(), call_id.to_string())
   - Used inside dispatcher loop for per-method errors

2. Define pub struct RequestError(pub StatusCode, pub JmapError) that implements axum::IntoResponse:
   - Serializes JmapError to JSON body
   - Sets Content-Type: application/json
   - Returns the given StatusCode

3. Define mapping fn error_status(err: &JmapError) -> StatusCode:
   - 'unknownCapability' → 400
   - 'invalidArguments' → 400
   - 'forbiddenMethod' → 403
   - 'accountNotFound' → 404
   - 'serverFail' → 500
   - All others → 400

4. Expose: pub fn request_error(err: JmapError) -> RequestError

Defensive programming rules:
- error_type strings must match RFC 8620 §7.1 exactly (already enforced by JmapError factory methods)
- description field omitted when None (serde skip_serializing_if already on JmapError)
- Method-level errors still return HTTP 200 (the error is inside methodResponses)
- Request-level errors return HTTP 4xx before any methodCalls are processed
- No PII (user IDs, IPs) in any error description

Tests:
- error_invocation('Contact/get', '0', JmapError::invalid_arguments('bad args')) serializes to ['Contact/get', {type:'invalidArguments',description:'bad args'}, '0']
- RequestError(400, JmapError::unknown_capability('x')) responds with HTTP 400 and correct JSON body
- error_status for each known type returns documented HTTP status
Oracle: RFC 8620 §7.1 error type strings and §3 invocation format, manually verified.
